newsitem.title: UK: Alliance & Leicester members vote for float.
newsitem.headline: Alliance & Leicester members vote for float.

text.p: Britain's Alliance & Leicester Building Society said on Tuesday it had received the required majorities of its investing and borrowing members in favour of conversion to a publicly listed company.

The mutual society, which until now has been owned by its borrowers and savers, plans to shed this status and float on the London Stock Exchange next year when every eligible member will receive an allocation of 250 shares.

"We are pleased that so many of our investing and borrowing members participated in the voting process and that a clear majority of those members voted in favour of conversion," the Alliance & Leicester's chief executive Peter White said.
The society said the flotation is expected to take place during the second quarter of 1997.

But the timetable has been thrown into some confusion by the fact that the British government has still not published a revised draft of its Building Society's bill, which could affect the society's status after it has gone public.
The flotation process has also attracted criticism from depositors with large accounts. They are angry they will be allocated the same number of free shares as those with much smaller accounts.
